study.title: John 4 - Jesus, the living water and the second sign in Cana
study.overview: John 4 shows Jesus crossing religious, social and regional barriers to reveal who he is and to offer life. The chapter unites three scenes: the meeting with the Samaritan woman, the reception of the Samaritans and the healing of the son of an officer in Cana. In all of them, the center is not the place, but the person of Jesus: he knows the human heart, gives the living water, is worshipped in spirit and in truth, and his word produces faith and life.

outline.title: Jesus leaves Judea and Samaria
outline.explanation: Upon learning of the reaction of the Pharisees, Jesus leaves Judea and proceeds to Galilee, passing through Samaria. The text highlights that he tires, sits by the well of Jacob and finds a Samaritan woman in a common but decisive moment.

outline.title: The Dialogue on Living Water and True Worship
outline.explanation: Jesus transforms a simple request for water into a revelation about the gift of God, human thirst, and eternal life. He also confronts the woman's moral history and corrects the discussion about the correct place of worship, pointing to worship the Father in spirit and in truth. The climax comes when he identifies himself as the Messiah.

outline.title: The testimony of the woman and the faith of the Samaritans
outline.explanation: The disciples strange the conversation, but the woman leaves her cantaro, goes to the city and calls the people. Jesus teaches that his true food is to do the will of the Father and speaks of the already mature harvest. Many Samaritans first believe by the testimony of the woman and then by the word of Jesus himself.

outline.title: Jesus returns to Galilee and performs the second sign in Cana
outline.explanation: After two days between the Samaritans, Jesus goes to Galilee. In Cana, an officer asks for the healing of his son, and Jesus calls him to believe without requiring physical presence. The man believes in the word of Jesus before seeing the result, and all his house believes too. John concludes that this was the second sign in Cana.

study.context: The chapter mentions Judea, Samaria and Galilee, regions of Jesus" ministry. The text also recalls the hostility between Jews and Samaritans, which makes dialogue with the well even more significant. The scenario of the well of Jacob and Cana refers to the memory of the people of Israel, but the narrative focus is not the geography itself; it is the progressive revelation of Jesus as the one who grants life and brings together people from different origins in the faith.
study.theology: John 4 teaches that Jesus not only offers something of God; he is the bearer of the gift of God. The image of the living water points to an inner and permanent satisfaction, which does not depend on rites or places. True worship is not bound to a mountain or to Jerusalem, because God is a spirit and sincere worshippers, guided by the truth revealed in Christ. The chapter also shows that faith can begin with a humble testimony, but must come to personal encounter with Jesus and trust in his word. Finally, the sign in Cana confirms that biblical faith does not first depend on seeing miracles; it responds to the word of Christ, and this response brings life to the whole house.

scholarViews.insight: The note understands the living water as a powerful image of the satisfaction that God grants, in contrast to the repeated thirst of the common water.
The note notes that Jesus went through Samaria doing good, and highlights the long conversation as a central part of his ministry between Jews and Samaritans.
The note draws attention to the second sign in Cana and sees it as a continuation of the first miracle done in that city.

questions: What still tries to satiate my spiritual thirst with things that leave again empty?
Have I worshipped God more by place, custom or tradition, or in spirit and truth, with sincerity and submission to the revelation of Christ?
Does my faith depend on visible signs, or do I trust the word of Jesus before I see the result?
study.practice: This week, take time for a simple and honest prayer, asking the Lord to reveal where you have sought to satiate your soul. Read John 4 in prayer and ask Jesus how the Samaritan woman should have answered: with openness, repentance and faith. He also seeks to bear witness to someone in a humble and direct way, telling what Christ has done in his life, without exaggeration or defensiveness. And practice worship with a focus on God, not on environmental preferences, remembering that the Father's presence is sought through the truth of Christ.
study.uncertainty: This study depends only on the chapter provided and the excerpts of commentators cited. It was not possible to confirm historical details beyond what the text itself mentions and what the notes support. Some confessional readings present in the notes were treated as interpretations, not as absolute conclusions of the text.
